html:
SMTO-AUT-0038 — SMTO can't use that name to find a Google account

GUID: 9b3adb1a-8374-5a12-8310-1e225cf0411e
Slug: google-parameter-reference-invalid
Domain: AUT · Subsystem: google-workspace

What happened

  • SMTO finds Google accounts and Google app settings only by their exact Parameter Store name, such as workspace. The name given was in a different form, like an email address, so nothing was looked up or changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Parameter Store from the More options menu and find the Google Workspace Account or Google Workspace OAuth App you want. Note its exact name. That saved name is the only thing SMTO accepts to pick a Google account or app.
  2. Ask again and refer to it by that name, typed after @ (for example @workspace) or picked from the list that appears when you type @. SMTO matches the name exactly and never guesses from an email address or a description.
  3. If you are choosing a name for a new connection, use only lowercase letters, numbers, dots and underscores, starting with a letter or number. Names in any other form are refused before anything is saved.

What success looks like

  • SMTO finds the account and the Google request or connection continues.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the name you used, to the person who manages SMTO's Google setup. Don't type the Google email address instead of the name; SMTO never looks accounts up by email.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Google account or OAuth app reference failed Parameter Store key parsing: after removing one leading @ it was not 1 to 160 characters of lowercase letters, digits, underscores or dots starting with a letter or digit.

What this means

  • Canonical Parameter Store key parsing rejected the supplied Google account/application reference. Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.

Why this can happen

  • Canonical Parameter Store key parsing rejected the supplied Google account/application reference.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the reference with the canonical stored key and permitted optional @ prefix.

How to fix it

  • Pass the exact normalized_key of the google_account or google_oauth_app record, optionally prefixed with @, as account_ref, account_key or auth_app_ref. Email addresses, display names, uppercase letters, hyphens and whitespace are rejected by account_key() and are never resolved as aliases.
  • Select the exact canonical Parameter Store key, optionally prefixed with @.

Retry and execution caution

  • Confirm account identity and required features before retrying.

How to verify the fix

  • The reference normalizes to the intended existing Parameter Store key.

What not to do

  • Do not expose client secrets, tokens, codes or PKCE verifiers.
  • Do not switch accounts or repeat uncertain mutations automatically.

Technical notes

  • Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
